new_statements.quote: [p. 18] 2. a rule raising stressed penultimate /ɑ/ to [ə], and … [p. 20] While all the factors involved in this rule are not known, it is clear that the raising of /ɑ/ to [ə] occurs only in stressed (i.e. penultimate) syllables, and that a morpheme boundary needs to be present. … In the penultimate syllable position (which is in general the stressed position), /ə/ is generally written as a, regardless of the context. … [p. 21] Penultimate stress rule for /ɑ/: banagami [bɑnɑ'ŋgəmi] 'strength' / nogamana [nəŋgɑ'mənɑ] 'his child' / wanis [wɑnis] 'three'
new_statements.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Jo Ann Conrad. 1987. 'The symbolization of /ə/ in Mufian (Southern Arapesh).' In John M. Clifton (ed.), Studies in Melanesian orthographies, 17-22. Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages 33. Ukarumpa: SIL.
new_statements.locator: printed pp. 18, 20 and 21 (PDF pp. 2, 4, 5); heading 'Penultimate stress rule for /ɑ/' on p. 21
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: 17-21 by eye. Printed p. 18 (PDF p. 2), item 2 of the list: 'a rule raising stressed penultimate /ɑ/ to [ə], and' — verbatim. Printed p. 20 (PDF p. 4), paragraph after (6): 'While all the factors involved in this rule are not known, it is clear that the raising of /ɑ/ to [ə] occurs only in stressed (i.e. penultimate) syllables, and that a morpheme boundary needs to be present.' — verbatim. Same page, last paragraph: 'In the penultimate syllable position (which is in general the stressed position), /ə/ is generally written as a, regardless of the context. This is based on the penultimate raising rule outlined above.' — verbatim. Printed p. 21 (PDF p. 5), heading 'Penultimate stress rule for…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog penultimate stress is penultimate stress; the paper states the same placement (penultimate = 'in general the stressed position') and adds the morphophonemic evidence that stress shifts to remain penultimate under suffixation. Balif (Central) dialect only.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable ('the penultimate syllable position (which is in general the stressed position)'); the paper's vowel-raising rule (/ɑ/ > [ə]) applies only in stressed = penultimate syllables. The transcribed examples in (4)-(6) and on p. 21 show the stress mark moving with suffixation so that it stays on the penult: [na'ŋgəmə] 'child' vs [nəŋgɑ'mənɑ] 'his child'; [bɑ'nɑŋgə] 'strong' vs [bɑnɑ'ŋgəmi] 'strength'; [i'fɑtə] 'water hole' vs [ifɑ'təl] 'water hole (poss.)'.
new_statements.exceptions: None listed; the placement is hedged as 'in general the stressed position'. The morpheme-boundary condition on p. 20 restricts the raising rule, not the stress rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Both listed works and the OPD describe the Balif (Central) dialect of Mufian: Conrad & Conrad 1987 p. 17 'This present study is restricted to the Balif (Central) dialect'; Alungum, Conrad & Lukas 1978 p. 90 'This study is based on the Central or Balif dialect' (the other dialects named are Begetef/Supari/Northern and Ilahita/Filifita/Southern). No source gives a stress statement for the other dialects.
